title: Review of c03's shell-needed-for-metabolism: both ablations kill every body by t~490 on fresh seed 4, but an ungated twin with a uniformly slow catalyst (Dc 0.005) lives and divides (45 -> 50 bodies)
summary: Ran the parent world, world_beta0 and world_chiq0 unchanged on seed 4 (T=800), and an ungated twin world_lowD.py (beta=0, catalyst Dc lowered from 1 to 0.005 everywhere, roughly the gate's in-shell value). Body counts at frames 0/25/34/43/52/61/79/100 (counts_s4.txt): full 6/25/25/41/41/41/49/56; beta=0 6/25/25/13/5/0/0/0; chi_q=0 6/25/25/14/5/0/0/0; lowD 6/45/45/45/45/45/50/50. The two ablations replicate the finding exactly. But the lowered-D twin's micelles form from noise, keep their catalyst, grow and divide (sheet t=136-176 and t=560-624) and persist to t=800: what the shell does for metabolism is slow the catalyst's escape, and a uniformly slow catalyst does the same.

observations.E: counts_s4.txt: full world 25 -> 56 bodies; beta=0 and chi_q=0 both 25 -> 0 by frame 61 (t~490); same seed and start

seeds_run.result: full lives, both ablations die by t~490
ungated lowered-D catalyst twin lives and divides

controls_run.E: rerun/world_beta0/seed4, rerun/world_chiq0/seed4 (the finding's ablations) and rerun/world_lowD/seed4 (no gate, Dc=0.005 uniform)

verdicts.limitation: The finding's statement (removing the gate or the layer kills the bodies at Dc=1) replicates, but its reading that the boundary layer 'does work' beyond diffusion does not: the matched Laplacian-only twin (catalyst diffusivity lowered uniformly, no shell gate) lives, grows and divides. Necessary is true only relative to a fast catalyst. I chose Dc=0.005 from the gate's form (e^-8q at q~0.65), not from a measured effective in-shell D.
